Issues.Title: Move source-build container to Azure Linux 4 after Arcade trailing-backslash fix
Issues.Body:
dotnet/aspnetcore#70522 moves aspnetcore's build and cross containers to Azure Linux 4. The source-build job stays on `azurelinux-3.0-net11.0-cross-amd64` for now because it fails on Azure Linux 4.

**Cause:** Arcade's `eng/common/core-templates/steps/source-build.yml` ends the build command with a trailing line continuation (`$portableBuildArgs \`). Azure Pipelines trims the script, so the generated file ends with a backslash and no newline:

- bash 5.2.15 (Azure Linux 3) drops the backslash.
- bash 5.3.9 (Azure Linux 4) passes a literal `\` argument to `build.sh`, and the build fails:

```
+ ./eng/build.sh --ci --configuration Release --restore --build --pack -bl --source-build --source-build -p:CrossBuild=true '\'
MSBUILD : error MSB1008: Only one project can be specified.
```

**Fix in Arcade:** https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/pull/17800 (dotnet/arcade#17800)

**Follow-up:** after that fix reaches aspnetcore through an Arcade update, move the source-build container to Azure Linux 4:

- `.azure/pipelines/ci.yml`: `azureLinuxCrossX64` → `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs:azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-amd64`
- `.azure/pipelines/ci-public.yml`: the source-build job's `container` → same image

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was generated with the help of GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Refresh the root npm workspace lockfile and add targeted tooling overrides for `debug`, `glob-parent`, modern `glob`/`minimatch`, `pacote`, and `uuid`. Updating `pacote` also replaces the old `sigstore` dependency graph.
- Inspect the branch's independent npm lockfiles as well as the root workspaces; no additional applicable dependency change is needed there. This branch does not contain the Vally evaluation-tools project.
- Mirror the resolved packages, including optional platform packages, into the public Azure npm feed.

The older callable `glob`/`minimatch` APIs are not replaced with incompatible modern exports. No test-framework migration or alert dismissal is included. This PR does not claim to resolve every npm finding: `extract-zip`, `deepmerge`, `braces`, and `sprintf-js` still have findings without published patched releases; other findings require broader tooling changes or separate assessment.

## Validation

- Anonymous clean install using Node 20.20.2 / npm 10.8.2.
- All workspace JavaScript builds pass; 22 Jest suites / 429 tests pass.
- Targeted dependency API checks pass, covering globs, watchers, UUID consumers, and local package manifests.
- Non-CI Blazor production build passes, including bundle-size reporting.
- SignalR lint passes. Blazor lint has the same 68 errors and 195 warnings as the original baseline; every diagnostic is identical.
- No .NET or browser integration tests were run.

Enforce JS unit-test failures in Npm.Workspace.nodeproj and JUnit CI tasks.

## Description

Ensures JavaScript/TypeScript Jest unit-test failures (as well as pre-JUnit lint/config/transform failures) reliably fail MSBuild and Azure Pipelines test publishing:

- **`eng/Npm.Workspace.nodeproj` (`_Test` target):**
  - Remove `ContinueOnError="true"` from `<Exec Command="npm run test" ... />` (matching `eng/Npm.Workspace.FunctionalTests.nodeproj`) so non-zero `npm run test` exit codes fail `_Test` directly with `error MSB3073`, including under direct `dotnet msbuild` and `-warnAsError 0` invocations rather than relying on `/warnaserror` promoting `warning MSB3073`.
  - Add `IgnoreStandardErrorWarningFormat="true"` so `console.error("Error: ...")` or `console.warn("Warning: ...")` output inside passing Jest tests is not misinterpreted as MSBuild canonical errors/warnings under `/warnaserror`.
- **`.azure/pipelines/jobs/default-build.yml` (public and internal `Publish js test results` steps):**
  - Set `failTaskOnFailedTests: true` on both `PublishTestResults@2` (`JUnit`) steps so failed tests recorded in `**/artifacts/log/**/*.junit.xml` fail the publish step instead of reporting green.
  - Set `continueOnError: ${{ parameters.continueOnError }}` to match `Run build.cmd` / `Run build.sh` in the same template (default `false` hard-fails PR/CI jobs, while internal `Windows_Test` preserves its `continueOnError: true` configuration from #61669).
  - Leave `failTaskOnMissingResultsFile` at its default (`false`) because `default-build.yml` shares `Publish js test results` with `isAzDOTestingJob: true` jobs that do not run JS unit tests (`Local_Windows`, `BlazorDailyTests`, `Windows_Stress_Test`).

### Validation

- `. .\activate.ps1; dotnet msbuild eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj /t:Test /p:RepoRoot="$PWD\"` with a simulated Jest assertion failure: **failed as expected** (`exit code 1`, `error MSB3073`, while emitting `<failure>` to `artifacts/log/win32.components-platform.junit.xml`; previously exited `0` with `warning MSB3073`).
- `.\eng\build.cmd -noBuildNative -noBuildManaged -noBuildJava -noRestore -noBuild -warnAsError 0 -test -projects eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj` with a simulated Jest assertion failure: **failed as expected** (`exit code 1`, `error MSB3073`).
- `. .\activate.ps1; dotnet msbuild eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj /t:Test /p:RepoRoot="$PWD\"` with a simulated pre-JUnit Jest config crash: **failed as expected** (`exit code 1`, `error MSB3073` with no `.junit.xml` emitted for the crashing workspace).
- `.\eng\build.cmd -noBuildNative -noBuildManaged -noBuildJava -noRestore -noBuild -test -projects eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj` with `console.error('Error: ...')` and `console.warn('Warning: ...')` in a passing Jest test under default `/warnaserror`: **passed** (`exit code 0`, `0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`).
- `.\eng\build.cmd -noBuildNative -noBuildManaged -noBuildJava -test -projects eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj`: **passed** (`exit code 0`, all 4 workspaces / 38 suites / 733 tests passed and emitted `win32.signalr.junit.xml`, `win32.components-webjs.junit.xml`, `win32.components-server-autopause.junit.xml`, and `win32.components-platform.junit.xml` with `failures="0" errors="0"`).
- `.\eng\build.cmd -noBuildNative -noBuildManaged -noBuildJava -noRestore -pack -projects eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj`: **passed** (`exit code 0`, produced `.tgz` packages).
- `. .\activate.ps1; dotnet msbuild eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj /t:Build /p:DesignTimeBuild=true /p:RepoRoot="$PWD\"`: **passed** (`exit code 0`).

Fixes #70517

Issues.Title: Harden JS unit-test failure enforcement in Npm.Workspace.nodeproj and AzDO JUnit publishing
Issues.Body:
More information on our issue management policies can be found here: https://aka.ms/aspnet/issue-policies

Please keep in mind that the GitHub issue tracker is not intended as a general support forum, but for reporting **non-security** bugs and feature requests.

If you believe you have an issue that affects the SECURITY of the platform, please do NOT create an issue and instead email your issue details to secure@microsoft.com. Your report may be eligible for our [bug bounty](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/msrc/bounty-dot-net-core) but ONLY if it is reported through email.
For other types of questions, consider using [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com).

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

JavaScript/TypeScript Jest unit-test failure enforcement has two gaps across MSBuild and Azure Pipelines:

1. **`eng/Npm.Workspace.nodeproj` (`_Test` target) sets `ContinueOnError="true"`:**
   ```xml
   <Target Name="_Test" BeforeTargets="Test">
     <Message Text="Testing NPM packages..." Importance="high" />
     <Exec Command="npm run test" ContinueOnError="true" WorkingDirectory="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory).." ConsoleToMsBuild="true" />
   </Target>
   ```
   `ContinueOnError="true"` (MSBuild `WarnAndContinue`) was added during the Yarn-to-npm workspace migration in #52914 (commit `ffd26877a4`; contrast `eng/Npm.Workspace.FunctionalTests.nodeproj:27`, which omits `ContinueOnError="true"`). Because `ContinueOnError="true"` downgrades non-zero `npm run test` exit codes to `warning MSB3073`, direct MSBuild invocations (`dotnet msbuild eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj /t:Test`), IDE builds, and wrapper builds with `-warnAsError 0` / `--warnaserror false` succeed (`exit code 0`) even when Jest unit tests fail or when `npm run test` exits non-zero before emitting JUnit XML (e.g., `pretest` ESLint or Jest config/transform errors). Wrapper builds without `-warnAsError 0` only failed indirectly because Arcade's `/warnaserror` flag promoted `warning MSB3073` back into an error. Additionally, `<Exec>` with `ConsoleToMsBuild="true"` did not set `IgnoreStandardErrorWarningFormat="true"`, allowing `Error: ...` or `Warning: ...` output from `console.error`/`console.warn` inside passing Jest tests to be parsed as MSBuild canonical errors/warnings.

2. **`.azure/pipelines/jobs/default-build.yml` omits `failTaskOnFailedTests: true` on JUnit publishing:**
   Both `Publish js test results` (`PublishTestResults@2`) steps in `.azure/pipelines/jobs/default-build.yml`—one in the public job template (`:308`) and one in the internal job template (`:570`)—run with `condition: always()` and omit `failTaskOnFailedTests: true` (which defaults to `false` in `PublishTestResults@2`). Consequently, the `Publish js test results` step succeeds green even when published `**/artifacts/log/**/*.junit.xml` reports contain `<failure>` or `<error>` entries.

### Expected Behavior

- `eng/Npm.Workspace.nodeproj`'s `_Test` target fails directly with `error MSB3073` whenever `npm run test` exits non-zero—regardless of whether `/warnaserror` is enabled—while ignoring canonical `Error:`/`Warning:` console text when `npm run test` exits `0` (`IgnoreStandardErrorWarningFormat="true"`).
- Both public and internal `Publish js test results` (`PublishTestResults@2`) steps in `.azure/pipelines/jobs/default-build.yml` set `failTaskOnFailedTests: true` (and `continueOnError: ${{ parameters.continueOnError }}` to match `Run build.cmd` / `Run build.sh` in the same template).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Introduce a failing assertion in a workspace Jest unit test (for example in `src/Components/Platform/src/js/test/Platform.test.ts`).
2. Run `. .\activate.ps1` and `dotnet msbuild eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj /t:Test /p:RepoRoot="$PWD\"` (or `.\eng\build.cmd -noBuildNative -noBuildManaged -noBuildJava -noRestore -noBuild -warnAsError 0 -test -projects eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj`).
3. Observe that `npm run test` exits with code `1` and writes `<failure>` to `artifacts/log/win32.components-platform.junit.xml`, but MSBuild logs `warning MSB3073` and exits `0`.

### Exceptions (if any)

```text
eng\Npm.Workspace.nodeproj(182,5): warning MSB3073: The command "npm run test" exited with code 1.
```

### .NET Version

12.0.100-alpha.1.26555.106

### Anything else?

- Surfaced during discussion on #70411 regarding whether JavaScript unit tests (`src/SignalR/clients/ts`, `src/Components/Web.JS`, `src/Components/Server.AutoPause/src/js`, `src/Components/Platform/src/js`) reliably gate CI.
- Note that `failTaskOnMissingResultsFile` on `PublishTestResults@2` should remain at its default (`false`) because `default-build.yml` shares `Publish js test results` with `isAzDOTestingJob: true` jobs that do not execute JS unit tests (`Local_Windows`, `BlazorDailyTests`, `Windows_Stress_Test`).

Issues.Title: AccessViolationException crashes w3wp on .NET 11 with IIS in-process hosting (SignalR hub invocation reads local endpoint in IISHttpContext.InitializeLocalEndpoint)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading a Blazor Web App (interactive server rendering) from .NET 10 to .NET 11.0.0, the IIS worker process is terminated by an `AccessViolationException` when it is hosted in-process. It happens during a SignalR hub method invocation (Blazor circuit traffic). After several crashes IIS rapid-fail protection stops the application pool and the site returns HTTP 503.

The faulting path is `DefaultHubDispatcher.StartActivity` → `ConnectionEndpointTags.AddConnectionEndpointTags` → `IConnectionEndPointFeature.LocalEndPoint` → `IISHttpContext.InitializeLocalEndpoint` → `NativeRequestContext.GetEndPoint` → `SocketAddress.CopyOutAddress`. The local endpoint is read lazily from the native request, apparently when that memory is no longer valid.

### Expected Behavior

No crash. Reading the connection endpoint for activity tags should not touch native request memory that has been released, or should fail safely.

### Steps To Reproduce

No minimal repro yet. Observed with:

1. A Blazor Web App using `AddInteractiveServerComponents()` / `AddInteractiveServerRenderMode()`, targeting `net11.0-windows`, published self-contained for `win-x64`.
2. Deployed to IIS with `hostingModel="inprocess"`.
3. Users open pages and interact; the worker process crashes with the stack below.

The same build on the same server with `hostingModel="outofprocess"` runs without the crash. The same application ran in-process on .NET 10 without it. The app does not register any OpenTelemetry or `ActivityListener` of its own.

Unverified guess: the invocation arrives on a connection whose originating HTTP request has already completed (for example the long-polling transport), so the native request backing `IISHttpContext` is gone when the endpoint is first read.

Issues.Title: Blazor browser options are ignored or applied incorrectly
Issues.Body:
Server-configured browser options were introduced by dotnet/aspnetcore#64807. These behaviors were found while reviewing dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs#38107. Reproduced with .NET SDK `11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148`. ### Circuit inactivity timeout In a Blazor Web App with an Interactive Server component on `/counter` and a static page on `/`, configure: ```csharp app.MapRazorComponents() .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode() .WithBrowserOptions(options => options.StaticServer.CircuitInactivityTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)); ``` Open `/counter`, navigate to `/` using enhanced navigation, and watch the `_blazor` WebSocket in the browser's Network tab. **Expected:** The circuit remains available for 10 minutes after its last interactive server root component is removed. **Actual:** The connection closes after about two seconds. Returning to `/counter` creates a new circuit. ### WebAssembly application culture Create a Blazor Web App with WebAssembly interactivity named `BrowserCultureRepro`. Configure its endpoint in `BrowserCultureRepro/Program.cs`: ```csharp app.MapRazorComponents() .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode() .AddAdditionalAssemblies(typeof(BrowserCultureRepro.Client._Imports).Assembly) .WithBrowserOptions(options => options.InteractiveWebAssembly.ApplicationCulture = "en-CA"); ``` Add `BrowserCultureRepro.Client/Pages/Culture.razor`: ```razor @page "/culture" @rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly @using System.Globalization

Running in browser: @OperatingSystem.IsBrowser()

Culture: @CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.Name

``` With the browser locale set to `en-US`, open `/culture` and wait for `Running in browser: True`. **Expected:** `Culture: en-CA`. **Actual:** `Culture: en-US`. ### DOM preservation In the Interactive Server app above, configure: ```csharp app.MapRazorComponents() .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode() .WithBrowserOptions(options => options.StaticServer.PreserveDom = false); ``` Open `/counter`, then use the Home link to navigate to `/`. **Expected:** DOM preservation is disabled and the browser performs a full page load. **Actual:** Enhanced navigation still runs and the same document is preserved. ### Interactive Server logging In the same app, configure: ```csharp app.MapRazorComponents() .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode() .WithBrowserOptions(options => options.LogLevel = LogLevel.Trace); ``` Open `/counter`, enable verbose messages in the browser console, and click the counter button. **Expected:** Debug messages such as `Dispatching event with handler id` appear. **Actual:** The circuit logger still uses the default warning level, so the debug message is missing. ### Reconnection retry interval In the same app, configure: ```csharp app.MapRazorComponents() .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode() .WithBrowserOptions(options => { options.InteractiveServer.ReconnectionMaxRetries = 2; options.InteractiveServer.ReconnectionRetryInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200); }); ``` Open `/counter`, set the browser offline, and run `Blazor._internal.forceCloseConnection()` in the browser console. Watch the failed `/_blazor/negotiate` requests. **Expected:** The two retry requests occur about 200 ms apart. **Actual:** They occur about one second apart. The option reaches the browser; this is a [reconnection timer behavior](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f79b2ab1de5dd66c4ab79b225658b7266edab9ef/src/Components/Web.JS/src/Platform/Circuits/DefaultReconnectionHandler.ts#L147-L199) that predates dotnet/aspnetcore#64807 and also affects the equivalent JavaScript option.

Issues.Title: Query-component validation (#68320) not backported to release/10.0: HTTP/2 :path query with SP/HTAB/CTL still accepted on .NET 10 LTS
Issues.Body:
## Summary

PR #68320 ("Validate the query component of the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 `:path` pseudo-header", commit a6dab8a1) is present on `main` and `release/11.0`, but `HttpCharacters.ContainsInvalidQueryChar` does not exist on `release/10.0`, and neither `Http2Stream.cs` nor `Http3Stream.cs` on that branch calls it.

.NET 10 is the current LTS (supported until 2028-11-14), so on the shipping LTS an HTTP/2 `:path` whose query component contains SP, HTAB or a CTL character is still accepted and handed to the application as `HttpRequest.QueryString`, where RFC 9113 section 8.3.1 requires such a request to be treated as malformed.

## Repro

Minimal app. The only non-default thing is an h2c endpoint, so a raw client can be used:

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core;
var b = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
b.WebHost.ConfigureKestrel(o => o.ListenLocalhost(5601, l => l.Protocols = HttpProtocols.Http2));
var app = b.Build();
app.Run(async ctx => await ctx.Response.WriteAsync($"QueryString={ctx.Request.QueryString.Value}"));
app.Run();
```

Raw HTTP/2 client, because curl percent-encodes these characters before they reach the wire:

```python
# python3 h2repro.py 5601 '/a?q=x y'
import socket, struct, sys
def frame(t, f, sid, p): return struct.pack(">I", len(p))[1:] + bytes([t, f]) + struct.pack(">I", sid) + p
def lit(b): return bytes([len(b)]) + b
def hdr(n, v): return b"\x00" + lit(n) + lit(v)
port, path = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2].encode("latin1").decode("unicode_escape").encode("latin1")
s = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=5)
s.sendall(b"PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n" + frame(0x4, 0, 0, b""))
s.sendall(frame(0x1, 0x4 | 0x1, 1, hdr(b":method", b"GET") + hdr(b":scheme", b"http")
          + hdr(b":authority", f"127.0.0.1:{port}".encode()) + hdr(b":path", path)))
buf = b""
try:
    while len(buf) < 4096:
        d = s.recv(65536)
        if not d: break
        buf += d
except socket.timeout: pass
i = 0
while i + 9 <= len(buf):
    ln = int.from_bytes(buf[i:i+3], "big"); t = buf[i+3]; pay = buf[i+9:i+9+ln]
    if t == 1: print("HEADERS (request accepted)")
    if t == 3: print("RST_STREAM code=" + str(int.from_bytes(pay[:4], "big")))
    i += 9 + ln
```

Observed with the same app binary, only the shared framework differs:

| `:path` | Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.14 | 11.0.0-rc.2.26508.107 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/a?q=x y` (SP) | HEADERS, request served | RST_STREAM code=1 |
| `/a?q=x\ty` (HTAB) | HEADERS, request served | RST_STREAM code=1 |
| `/a?q=x\x01y` | HEADERS, request served | RST_STREAM code=1 |
| `/a?q=x\x7fy` (DEL) | HEADERS, request served | RST_STREAM code=1 |
| `/a? ` | HEADERS, request served | RST_STREAM code=1 |
| `/a?q=x%20y` (valid) | HEADERS, request served | HEADERS, request served |

On 10.0.14 the application sees the raw character in `HttpRequest.QueryString`.

## Branch state

| branch | `ContainsInvalidQueryChar` in `HttpCharacters.cs` | called from `Http2Stream.cs` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | present | yes |
| release/11.0 | present | yes |
| release/10.0 | absent | no |

release/9.0 and release/8.0 both reached end of support on 2026-11-10, so they are not part of this request.

## Scope, and what I did not verify

I measured HTTP/2 only. HTTP/3 receives the identical change in `Http3Stream.cs` in the same PR, but I did not exercise it.

I did not find a downstream exploit for this. Forwarding such a request through YARP 2.3 percent-encodes the characters (`%20`, `%09`, `%01`, `%7F`) into the HTTP/1.1 request target, so it is not a request-line injection there. I am filing this as a conformance and servicing question, not as a security report.

## Ask

Please consider servicing PR #68320 into release/10.0.

Happy to provide any further detail if useful.

Issues.Title: Apache RewriteCond negation is incorrectly applied to string and integer comparisons
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Describe the bug ASP.NET Core URL Rewrite accepts Apache `RewriteCond` comparison patterns prefixed with `!`, but does not correctly negate their results. For string comparisons, `RuleBuilder` passes the parsed negation flag to `StringMatch` as its `ignoreCase` argument. For integer comparisons, the negation flag is ignored. Consequently, `!=https` and `!-eq1` behave as positive equality rather than negated equality, causing the associated rule to execute for the wrong requests. ### Expected Behavior A leading `!` should negate the comparison result, independently of case-sensitivity flags. For example: - `%{REQUEST_SCHEME} !=https` should match HTTP, not HTTPS. - `%{QUERY_STRING} !-eq1` should match `2`, not `1`. ### Steps To Reproduce Configure the middleware before the terminal endpoint: ```csharp var rules = """ RewriteCond %{REQUEST_SCHEME} !=https RewriteRule ^/probe$ - [F] """; app.UseRewriter( new RewriteOptions().AddApacheModRewrite(new StringReader(rules))); app.Run(context => context.Response.WriteAsync("Endpoint reached")); ``` Expose HTTP and HTTPS listeners and request `/probe` through each, without automatically following redirects:
Request | Expected status | Actual status -- | -- | -- HTTP /probe | 403 | 200 HTTPS /probe | 200 | 403
Replacing `!=https` with positive `=https` produces the same actual outcomes. Replacing it with negated regex `!^https$` produces the expected outcomes. The integer comparison reproduces separately with: ``` RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} !-eq1 RewriteRule ^/probe$ - [F] ```
Request | Expected status | Actual status -- | -- | -- /probe?1 | 200 | 403 /probe?2 | 403 | 200

The -ne1 control produces the expected outcomes.

### Exceptions (if any) None. The rules parse successfully but evaluate incorrectly. ### .NET Version The reproduction used the .NET 10.0.14 runtime, with Rewrite compiled directly from the repository sources. ### Anything else? Relevant implementation: - `ConditionPatternParser.ParseActionCondition` preserves leading `!` in `Invert`. - `RuleBuilder.AddConditionFromParts` passes `Invert` as string comparison’s `ignoreCase` argument and omits it from integer comparison construction. The reproduction used real HTTP/TLS requests, not manually assigned `Request.Scheme` values.

Issues.Title: Inserting a MarkupString with many top-level nodes is quadratic since .NET 11 (insertLogicalChild orphan scan)
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Describe the bug Since .NET 11, inserting a `MarkupString` with many top-level nodes is quadratic in the number of nodes. `insertLogicalChild` in `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/LogicalElements.ts` gained an orphan-removal loop in #66007 ("Fix Blazor crash when interactive component is in layout with enhanced nav"). The loop walks the **whole** logical-children array of the parent on **every** call: ```ts const newSiblings = getLogicalChildrenArray(parent); for (let i = newSiblings.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { const sibling = newSiblings[i] as any as Node; if (!sibling.parentNode) { ... } } ``` `BrowserRenderer.insertMarkup` calls `insertLogicalChild` once per top-level node of the parsed markup, into the same container, so inserting markup with n top-level nodes does about n²/2 sibling checks. ### Expected Behavior Inserting a large `MarkupString` costs about the same as on .NET 10. ### Steps To Reproduce Render a `MarkupString` holding many top-level elements, for example the HTML Markdig produces for a 1.2 MB Markdown document of short paragraphs (about 18,000 `

` elements, 1.3 MB of HTML), in a Blazor Server component. Measured with the server's own `RemoteRenderer` log (`Completing batch N without error in X ms`, which runs when the browser confirms the batch), same machine, same 1,309,606-byte render batch, nothing else running: | Runtime | Batch confirmed after | | --- | --- | | .NET 10 (ASP.NET Core 10.0.x) | 47 ms | | .NET 11 (ASP.NET Core 11.0.0) | 8,700 ms | | .NET 11, same HTML inside one `

` (one top-level node) | 23 ms | Under CPU load the .NET 11 case took 18.75 s. ### Workaround Wrap the markup in a single root element, so `insertMarkup` inserts one node and the browser's parser builds the rest. ### Possible fix Do the orphan sweep once per `insertMarkup` (or per render batch) rather than inside each `insertLogicalChild`, or only when the computed `nextSibling` is actually disconnected. ### .NET Version 11.0.100 ### Anything else? The same script is used by Blazor Hybrid (`BlazorWebView`), so MAUI and WPF/WinForms hosts are affected as well.

# Fix Blazor Server navigation during circuit startup

Keep Blazor Server navigation in sync during circuit startup.

## Description

This change addresses enhanced navigation that occurs while a Server circuit is starting.

### Root cause

The circuit starts with the current browser URL. If enhanced navigation happens before the Server renderer attaches, the location change is not sent to the circuit. As a result, the circuit can retain the old URL.

### Fix

- Save the URL used to start the circuit.
- When the Server renderer attaches, compare it with the current browser URL and send an update if it changed.
- Handle send failures through the existing circuit error path.

### Before Fix

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d124d709-6645-4f12-9533-5c200f850c15



### After Fix

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec0b5fbc-566f-4053-8be8-a30e40031be8



### Test case

Added an E2E test that delays renderer attachment, performs enhanced navigation, and checks the server URL and query-bound state after attachment.

Issues.Title: Prevent obsolete circuit resumes after enhanced navigation to static SSR.
Issues.Body: ## Description Fixes a circuit-lifetime race reported in #69869. After enhanced navigation from an Interactive Server page to a static SSR page, hiding and showing the tab can resume a circuit that has already been disposed. Subsequent navigation to an interactive page can leave it without a working circuit and report: ```text The circuit associated with this dispatcher is no longer available. ``` ### Root cause Automatic pause retained state belonging to a retired circuit. Entry-point checks alone also missed resumes already waiting for connection startup or a `ResumeCircuit` reply. Disposal could stop the old connection and disconnect the old circuit ID before resume assigned a new connection or received a newly created server circuit ID. The continuation could then publish circuit-opened, connection-up, and component-reload notifications on a retired manager. ### Changes - Notify automatic pause synchronously when the circuit is retired; invalidate obsolete continuations and clear pending timers, pause deferrals, and idle waits. - Make disposal once-only and reentrant-safe. - Clear only an outstanding pause display during disposal; log a custom cleanup callback failure without skipping transport/server teardown. - Reject pause and resume requests once disposal starts, and suppress reconnect UI during disposal while retaining disconnect-beacon suppression. - Track the full resume operation, including connection startup and notifications. Drain it before final teardown, including when resume fails. - Adopt a returned circuit ID before terminal handling so disposal stops the current connection and disconnects the correct server circuit. - Suppress subsequent resume notifications after asynchronous or callback-initiated retirement. - Extend the existing manager, automatic-pause, and enhanced-navigation test suites. No new public API or server protocol changes. ### Output **Before:** **After:** Fixes: #69869

Issues.Title: Fix retained references during Blazor renderer and WebView disposal
Issues.Body: ## Description Disposed renderers could retain components through event-handler bindings and non-fixed cascading subscriptions. Disposed WebView managers could also retain their current page context. This change: - Clears renderer event bindings and event-handler replacement mappings during disposal. - Moves cascading-parameter unsubscription into `ComponentState.DisposeAsync`, covering whole-renderer teardown while preserving cleanup during normal component removal. - Clears the WebView manager's current page context in a `finally` block, including when disposal throws. - Preserves disposal exception propagation and existing renderer exception aggregation. - Adds focused regression tests and preservation controls. No public API signatures are added or changed. The intended behavioral change is releasing references after disposal. ## Root Cause Three cleanup paths left references behind: 1. **Renderer event dictionaries:** renderer disposal cleared component-state dictionaries but retained event bindings and replacement-ID mappings. 2. **Cascading subscriptions:** unsubscription occurred in `DisposeInBatchAsync`, but whole-renderer teardown called `ComponentState.DisposeAsync` directly, bypassing that cleanup. 3. **WebView page context:** disposing the current page context did not clear the manager's reference to it. The fix performs cleanup at the existing lifecycle owners without changing the overall disposal structure. ## Testing Added coverage in `RendererDisposalTest`: - `DisposedRenderer_ReleasesComponentWithoutEventHandler` - `DisposedRenderer_ReleasesComponentWithEventHandler` - `DisposedRenderer_ReleasesComponentWithFixedCascadingValue` - `DisposedRenderer_ReleasesComponentWithNonFixedCascadingValue` - `DisposedRenderer_ClearsEventHandlerReplacementsBeforeDisplayCompletes` Added coverage in `WebViewManagerTests`: - `DisposingWebViewManager_ReleasesCurrentPageContext` - `DisposingWebViewManager_ReleasesCurrentPageContextWhenScopeDisposalThrows` The collection tests keep the suspected retaining owner alive and clear captured test batches that would otherwise introduce test-only roots. The replacement-ID test uses an explicit incomplete display task rather than a timing delay. The exceptional-disposal test also verifies that the original exception propagates unchanged. ### Before/after verification - Event-handler component retention, non-fixed cascading subscription retention, and normal WebView page-context retention failed before the fix and passed afterward. - An isolated counterfactual removing replacement-map cleanup failed the pending-display test at the empty-dictionary assertion; restoring cleanup passed. - An isolated counterfactual clearing the page context only after successful disposal failed the exceptional-disposal test at the null-context assertion; restoring `finally` passed. - No-handler and fixed-cascade cases passed as preservation controls. These paired checks were performed earlier in the investigation. The following targeted suites were subsequently rerun successfully. ### Components renderer and cascading tests From the repository root, activate the repository SDK: ```powershell . .\activate.ps1 ``` ```powershell dotnet test .\src\Components\Components\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Tests.csproj ` -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false ` --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Test.RendererTest.|FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Test.CascadingParameterTest.|FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Test.RendererDisposalTest." ` --verbosity quiet ` --logger "console;verbosity=normal" ``` Result: **182 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; exit code 0**. This selection includes existing renderer disposal, exception-handling, and cascading-parameter tests. ### WebView manager tests ```powershell dotnet test .\src\Components\WebView\WebView\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView.Test.csproj ` -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false ` --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView.WebViewManagerTests." ` --verbosity quiet ` --logger "console;verbosity=normal" ``` Result: **13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; exit code 0**. Both commands ran sequentially with normal builds; neither used `--no-build`. ### Manual Validation **Interactive Blazor sample** - Exercised an in-tree Interactive Server sample across 10 post-fix runs. - Confirmed component disposal and collection while retaining the relevant owners. - Removed the temporary sample after validation. **Native WPF BlazorWebView** - Built a .NET 12 Windows probe referencing the in-tree framework. - Confirmed five framework DLLs matched the source-built assemblies by hash and inspected runtime assembly locations. - Verified button interaction and a non-fixed cascading value update from `123` to `456`. - Disposed the native WebView and observed exactly one component disposal callback. - Confirmed the manager's page context was cleared. - Confirmed the component became collectible while deliberately retaining the disposed manager, renderer, and cascading source. Native validation consists of one successful post-fix WPF run. It is not native pre-fix/post-fix proof or MAUI-specific lifecycle validation. Fixes dotnet/aspnetcore#70393

Issues.Title: Remember me isPersistent understanding
Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)

Apologize if my feedback may sound controversial or may spark a debate.

I need to be sure that the problem mentioned on this [page](https://github.com/aspnet/Tooling/blob/master/known-issues-vs2017.md#to-create-aspnet-core-10--11-projects-install-visual-studios-net-core-10---11-developer-tools-for-web-component) about .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling is installed when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project should not happen or should not be supported in VS 2019.

1. VS 2019 is about to be released in around early 2019
2. ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 is not going to be supported anymore, based on [this page](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/master/microsoft-support.md).
3. Creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 will always install the .NET Core 1.0/1.1 web tooling, and this is not necessary when previous reason has reached the unsupported period and it's quite near or might be the same time of VS 2019 release.
4. Based on the problem mentioned above, VS 2017 has no "built in" tooling when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project, but the external tooling may help. Therefore for those that still need to maintain ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 projects, we could use VS 2017 as long as the VS 2017 is still in support lifecycle or in mainstream support lifecycle.

I welcome feedback 🙂

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time" (#537)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.FindByLoginAsync`
- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.RemoveLoginAsync`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

## Current support policy

ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages (latest patched version only) are currently [supported](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/aspnet#dotnet-core) on .NET Framework, following the support cycle for those .NET Framework versions. After April 13, 2027, this support will end regardless of the .NET Framework version in use.

Note that the [ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/aspnet/2.3-packages) include the Entity Framework 2.3 packages, which will end support on the same date.

## Impact of end of support

After ASP.NET Core 2.3 reaches end of support:

- No new security updates will be issued for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- Continuing to use an unsupported version may expose your applications to security vulnerabilities.
- Technical support will no longer be available for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- The ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages will be deprecated.

## Upgrade recommendation

We recommend upgrading to a [currently supported version of .NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet), such as .NET 10 (LTS).

To help with the upgrade process, we recommend using [GitHub Copilot modernization](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/porting/github-copilot-app-modernization/overview), which provides AI-powered assistance to help you analyze, plan, and execute your migration to a modern .NET version.

Automates creation of documentation tracking issues in `dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs` when breaking change issues are opened or labeled in this repository.

**New workflow:** `.github/workflows/create-docs-issue.yaml`

Multi-layer detection to handle race conditions and partial failures:
- Checks for existing bot comments in source issue
- Searches docs repo by title before creating

Separate try-catch blocks for each operation:

- Comment posting failures → don't fail workflow (docs issue already created)
- Permission errors → explicit message about `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` requirement

Configure `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` repository secret with `repo` scope for cross-repository issue creation. Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` but will fail with clear error message.

Explicit minimal permissions: `issues: write`, `contents: read`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Deprecating WebHostBuilder,  IWebHost, and WebHost
Issues.Body:
### Description

`WebHostBuilder` was replaced by `HostBuilder` ([generic host](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder)) in 3.0 and we also added [`WebApplicationBuilder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) in 6.0.

We are now marking `WebHostBuilder` as obsolete to encourage users to move on to the alternatives which is where future investments will occur, and we're also marking `IWebHost` and `WebHost` as deprecated to clean up other parts of the now obsolete web host story.

### Version

.NET 10 RC 1

### Previous behavior

```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

### New behavior

Using `WebHostBuilder` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR004**:
> warning ASPDEPR004: WebHostBuilder is deprecated in favor of HostBuilder and WebApplicationBuilder. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/004.

Using `IWebHost` or `WebHost` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR008**:
> warning ASPDEPR008: WebHost is obsolete. Use HostBuilder or WebApplicationBuilder instead. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/008.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [x] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

We recommend the use of `HostBuilder` and `WebApplication` going forward over `WebHostBuilder` because they have all the features of `WebHostBuilder` and will be the focus of future investment.

### Recommended action

See https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/host/generic-host or https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication for more details on the different hosting models. As well as [HostBuilder replaces WebHostBuilder](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder) and [Introducing WebApplication](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) for migration guides.

Below is an example of converting `WebHostBuilder` to `HostBuilder`:

**Before**
```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

**After**
```csharp
using var host = new HostBuilder()
    .ConfigureWebHost(webHostBuilder =>
    {
        webHostBuilder
            .UseTestServer() // If using TestServer
            .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
            .UseStartup()
            .UseKestrel();
    })
    .Build();
await host.StartAsync();

var testServer = host.GetTestServer();
```

Both Copilot and ChatGpt have given good results so far when asked to convert a WebHostBuilder example to use HostBuilder. Below is an example prompt:
<details>
<summary>Example AI Prompt</summary>

> Can you convert
>
> var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
>     .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
>     .UseStartup()
>     .UseKestrel();
> // Test code might use TestServer:
> var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
>
> to use HostBuilder.

</details>

### Affected APIs

`public class Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.WebHostBuilder`
`public interface Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHost`
`public static class Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebHost`

### Discussion

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/63480

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Exception diagnostics are suppressed when `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true
Issues.Body:
### Description

The [ASP.NET Core exception handler middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#exception-handler-page), `UseExceptionHandler()`, is responsible for catching and processing unhandled exceptions from ASP.NET Core requests.

In .NET 8, we introduced [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#iexceptionhandler). Implementations of `IExceptionHandler` are registered with dependency injection and invoked by the middleware. An implementation can return `true` from `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` to indicate that the exception has been handled. The middleware stops processing the exception once it has been handled.

In .NET 10, we're changing the default behavior so that the middleware no longer records diagnostics for exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

The exception handler middleware recorded diagnostics about exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

The exception diagnostics are:

- Logging `UnhandledException` to `ILogger`.
- Writing the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HandledException` event to `EventSource`.
- Adding the `error.type` tag to the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

### New behavior

If `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns `true`, then exception diagnostics are no longer recorded by default.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

ASP.NET Core users have given feedback that the previous behavior was undesirable. Their `IExceptionHandler` implementation reported that the exception was handled, but the error handling middleware still recorded the error in the app's telemetry.

We are changing ASP.NET Core to follow the behavior expected by users by suppressing diagnostics when `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. We're also adding configuration options to customize exception diagnostics behavior if needed.

### Recommended action

If you want handled exceptions to continue recording telemetry, you can use the new `ExceptionHandlerOptions.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback` option:

```cs
app.UseExceptionHandler(new ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = context => false;
});
```

The context passed to the callback includes information about the exception, the request, and whether the exception was handled. Returning `false` from the callback indicates that diagnostics shouldn't be suppressed. This restores the previous behavior.

### References

- Issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54554
- PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59074

### Affected APIs

- `UseExceptionHandler()`
- `IExceptionHandler`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and MVC API analyzers are deprecated
Issues.Body:
## Description

The `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` MSBuild property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. When `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will now emit warning `ASPDEPR007`.

## Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

## Previous behavior

Previously, developers could set `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` in their Web SDK projects to enable MVC API analyzers without any warnings or deprecation notices.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
    <IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

The project would build successfully without any deprecation warnings.

## New behavior

Starting in .NET 10 Preview 7, when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will emit warning `ASPDEPR007`:

```
warning ASPDEPR007: The IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
```

The analyzers will continue to function, but developers will receive this deprecation warning during compilation.

## Type of breaking change

- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

## Reason for change

## Reason for change

The MVC API analyzers were originally introduced to help keep return types and attributes in sync for API controllers, ensuring consistency between method signatures and their corresponding OpenAPI documentation. These analyzers provided compile-time validation to catch mismatches between declared return types and the actual types returned by controller actions.

However, with the introduction of Minimal APIs and the `TypedResults` pattern, the .NET ecosystem has evolved toward a more type-safe approach for API development. `TypedResults` provides compile-time guarantees about response types without requiring additional analyzers, making the MVC API analyzers redundant for modern .NET applications. In .NET 10, `TypedResults` are supported in controller-based APIs.

**Previous approach with MVC API analyzers:**
```csharp
[HttpGet]
[ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)]
[ProducesResponseType(404)]
public async Task<ActionResult> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    if (product == null)
        return NotFound(); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType(404)
    
    return Ok(product); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)
}
```

**Or with controller actions using TypedResults:**
```csharp
[HttpGet("{id}")]
public async Task<Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    return product == null 
        ? TypedResults.NotFound() 
        : TypedResults.Ok(product);
}
```

The `TypedResults` pattern eliminates the need for separate analyzers because the return type itself (`Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>`) explicitly declares all possible response types at compile time. This approach is more maintainable, provides better IntelliSense support, and automatically generates accurate OpenAPI documentation without additional tooling.

As the .NET ecosystem continues to embrace `TypedResults` as the recommended pattern for API development, the MVC API analyzers have become obsolete and are being deprecated to streamline the development experience.

## Recommended action

Developers should:

1. **Remove the deprecated property**: Remove `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` from your project files to eliminate the warning.

2. **Suppress the warning temporarily**: If you need to continue using the deprecated analyzers temporarily, you can suppress the warning:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);ASPDEPR007</NoWarn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

3. **Migrate to TypedResults**: Migrate to the `TypedResults` pattern documented above to ensure better consistency between application behavior and OpenAPI documentation.

## Affected APIs

- MSBuild property: `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers`
- Associated MVC API analyzers included when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is `true`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Forwarded Headers Middleware Now Ignores X-Forwarded-* Headers from Unknown Proxies
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 8.0.17 and 9.0.6, the Forwarded Headers Middleware will ignore all `X-Forwarded-*` headers from proxies that are not explicitly configured as trusted.

### Version

.NET 8

### Previous behavior

Previously, the middleware, when not configured to use `X-Forwarded-For`, would process `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and `X-Forwarded-Host` headers from any source, potentially allowing malicious or misconfigured proxies/clients to spoof these headers and affect your application's understanding of client information.

### New behavior

With this change, only headers sent by known, trusted proxies (as configured via `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownProxies` and `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownNetworks`) will be processed. Headers from unknown sources will be ignored.

**This is a breaking change**: If your deployment relied on forwarded headers from proxies not configured in your application's trusted proxy list, those headers will no longer be honored.

This can cause behavior like infinite redirects if you're using the Https redirection middleware and using TLS termination in your proxy. Or authentication to fail if using TLS termination and expecting an https request.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The change was made for security hardening, as the proxy and IP lists weren't being applied in all cases.

### Recommended action

- **Review your deployment topology:**  
  Ensure that all legitimate proxy servers in front of your app are properly added to `KnownProxies` or `KnownNetworks` in your `ForwardedHeadersOptions` configuration.
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownProxies = { IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_PROXY_IP") }
  });
  ```
  Or, for a network:
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownNetworks = { new IPNetwork(IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_NETWORK_IP"), PREFIX_LENGTH) }
  });
  ```

- **If you wish to enable previous behavior:**  
  You may need to relax your configuration, but this is **not recommended** due to security risks. You can do this by clearing the `KnownNetworks` and `KnownProxies` lists in `ForwardedHeadersOptions` to allow any proxy or network to forward these headers.

You can also set the `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` environment variable to true, which clears the lists and enables `ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto`.

For applications targeting .NET 9.0 or less, you can set the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides.IgnoreUnknownProxiesWithoutFor` [AppContext](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/runtime-libraries/system-appcontext) switch to `"true"` or `1` to get back to the previous behavior. Alternatively, set the `MICROSOFT_ASPNETCORE_HTTPOVERRIDES_IGNORE_UNKNOWN_PROXIES_WITHOUT_FOR` environment variable.

> [!Note]
> In cloud environments, the proxy IP(s) can change over the lifetime of the app and `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` is sometimes used to make forwarded headers work.

### References

- [Forwarded Headers Middleware documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/proxy-load-balancer)

### Affected APIs

`UseForwardedHeaders();`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: dev cert export no longer creates folder
Issues.Body:
### Description

When you export the ASP.NET Core development certificate (used to enable https in local development), it will no longer create the directory into which the certificate is being exported, if that directory doesn’t already exist.

This change first appears in 8.0.10 and 9.0 RC1.

### Version

.NET 8 GA

### Previous behavior

```
dotnet dev-certs https -ep C:\NonExistent\cert.pfx
```

If `C:\NonExistent\` did not exist when the command was run, it would be created (with permissions inherited from the containing directory).

### New behavior

The target directory must exist or the export will fail with a message like `There was an error exporting the HTTPS developer certificate to a file.`

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The development certificate is exported with its private key, so unauthorized access can be very problematic.  It may, nevertheless, be necessary to make it readable to multiple accounts - e.g. if the consuming process will not be run as the current user.  Rather than attempting to determine (and securely establish) permissions for the target directory, `dotnet dev-certs` require that it already exist.

### Recommended action

Create the target directory (with appropriate permissions) before invoking `dotnet dev-certs`.

### Affected APIs

This functionality is not presently exposed via an API - it is invoked from the command line.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Handling of middleware types with multiple constructors
Issues.Body:
### Description

Formerly, when a middleware type with multiple satisfiable constructors was instantiated from the dependency injection container, the one with the most parameters would be used.  Now that only happens if the dependency injection container implements [`IServiceProviderIsService`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/microsoft.extensions.dependencyinjection.iserviceproviderisservice).

### Version

.NET 9 RC 1

### Previous behavior

Formerly, the first constructor was preferred (when both were satisfied) because it has more parameters.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: DefaultKeyResolution.ShouldGenerateNewKey has a slightly altered meaning
Issues.Body:
### Description

`DefaultKeyResolution.ShouldGenerateNewKey` no longer reflects whether the default key is close to its expiration time.

### Version

.NET 9 Preview 3

### Previous behavior

It was an undocumented, but consistent, feature of the API that `ShouldGenerateNewKey` would be true if the default key was within two days (an over-simplification) of its expiration time.  The amount of lead time was based on the polling interval of `ICacheableKeyRingProvider`, which was not something `IDefaultKeyResolver.ResolveDefaultKeyPolicy` should have depended upon (since, for example, alternative implementations would probably not be aware of these details).

### New behavior

If `ShouldGenerateNewKey` is true, it now indicates that either there is no default key or that for some other policy reason (i.e. in a specialized implementation of `IDefaultKeyResolver`, a new key should be generated.  The `ICacheableKeyRingProvider` will make its own decision about whether the expiration time is close enough to warrant generating a new key.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

First, we wanted to change the logic around key generation near expiration time and, second, this makes it more straightforward to implement a custom `IDefaultKeyResolver`.

Note that the documentation for this type already states that "This API supports infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code. This API may change or be removed in future releases."

### Recommended action

If you have an `IDefaultKeyResolver` implementation that tries to replicate the expiry logic, that logic can be removed (however, leaving it is fine as well).

If you were consuming `IDefaultKeyResolver` directly, for the express purpose of determining whether expiration was pending and that continues to be important, you can the default key's `ExpirationDate` property directly.

### Affected APIs

Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection.KeyManagement.Internal.DefaultKeyResolution.ShouldGenerateNewKey

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Minimal APIs consuming IFormFile or IFormFileCollection parameters require anti-forgery checks
Issues.Body:
### Description

Minimal API endpoints that consume an `IFormFile` or `IFormFileCollection` will now be opted-in to requiring anti-forgery token validation using the new anti-forgery middleware.

### Version

.NET 8 RC 1

### Previous behavior

Minimal API endpoints that bound a parameter from the form via `IFormFile` or `IFormFileCollection` did not require anti-forgery validation.

### New behavior

Minimal API endpoints that bound a parameter from the form via `IFormFile` or `IFormFileCollection` did require anti-forgery validation. An exception will be thrown if the anti-forgery middleware is not registered for an API that defines these input types.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Anti-forgery token validation is a recommended security precaution for APIs that consume data from a form.

### Recommended action

Users can opt out of anti-forgery validation for specific endpoints by using the `DisableAntiforgery` method like so:

```csharp
var app = WebApplication.Create();

app.MapPost("/", (IFormFile formFile) => ...)
  .DisableAntiforgery();

app.Run();
```

### Affected APIs

None.
